question: What is generally produced when a metal reacts with an acid?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Salt and hydrogen gas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a **metal** reacts with a **dilute acid**, it generally produces a **metal salt** and **hydrogen gas**. This is a characteristic chemical property of most reactive metals.
 
• In this chemical process, the **metal** displaces the **hydrogen** atoms from the **acid** molecules. For example, when **Zinc** reacts with **Hydrochloric acid**, **Zinc Chloride** and **Hydrogen gas** are formed. ***Hence, the statement regarding salt and hydrogen gas production is correct.***
 
• The general chemical equation for this reaction can be represented as: **Metal + Dilute Acid → Salt + Hydrogen Gas (H2)**.
 
• The evolution of **hydrogen gas** can be tested using a burning splinter. When the splinter is brought near the mouth of the test tube where the reaction is occurring, the gas burns with a characteristic **"pop" sound**.
 
• The rate of this reaction depends on the **reactivity** of the metal. Highly reactive metals like **Sodium (Na)** and **Potassium (K)** react explosively, while less reactive metals like **Iron (Fe)** react more slowly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reactivity Series influence**: Metals that are positioned above **hydrogen** in the **reactivity series** (like **Magnesium, Aluminum, Zinc, and Iron**) can displace hydrogen from acids. However, metals below hydrogen, such as **Copper (Cu)**, **Silver (Ag)**, and **Gold (Au)**, do not typically react with dilute acids like **HCl** or **H2SO4** to produce hydrogen gas.
 
• **The Nitric Acid Exception**: When metals react with **Nitric acid (HNO3)**, **hydrogen gas** is usually not evolved. This is because **Nitric acid** is a **strong oxidizing agent**. It oxidizes the hydrogen gas produced into **water (H2O)** and itself gets reduced to various nitrogen oxides such as **N2O, NO, or NO2**.
 
• **Exceptions to the Nitric Acid Rule**: Only very dilute **Nitric acid** reacts with **Magnesium (Mg)** and **Manganese (Mn)** to actually evolve **hydrogen gas**.
 
• **Types of Salts**: The type of salt formed depends on the acid used. **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** yields **Metal Chlorides**, **Sulfuric acid (H2SO4)** yields **Metal Sulfates**, and **Acetic acid** yields **Metal Acetates**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Displacement Reaction**: This reaction is a prime example of a **single displacement reaction**, specifically a **redox reaction**, where the metal is **oxidized** (loses electrons) and the hydrogen ions in the acid are **reduced** (gain electrons) to form neutral hydrogen gas.
 
• **Exothermic Nature**: The reaction between a metal and an acid is generally **exothermic**, meaning it is accompanied by the release of **heat energy**. The temperature of the reaction mixture usually rises during the process.
 
• **Practical Application**: This reaction is commonly used in **laboratories** for the **preparation of hydrogen gas** on a small scale, typically using **granulated zinc** and **dilute sulfuric acid**.
 
• **Safety Fact**: Because **hydrogen** is highly **inflammable** and forms explosive mixtures with air, these reactions must be performed with caution in controlled environments.
 
• **Corrosion**: This chemical principle explains why **acidic food substances** (like curd or lemon juice) should not be stored in **copper** or **brass** vessels, as the acid reacts with the metal to produce **toxic salts**.
